# The tasks.json command that runs a file presenting as a WOFF2 font through
# node. There is no legitimate reason to execute a font file as JavaScript.
# The .vscode/tasks.json path itself stays out of filenames.txt because it is
# legitimate in most repositories; this command string is the part that is not.
# Source: OpenSourceMalware, "A Developer's Guide to Getting Rid of
# PolinRider", August 2026.
node ./public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2
#
# NullReceiver: the campaign marker and the sending wallet. The technique reads
# its C2 out of the recipient address of a zero-value, zero-data Ethereum
# transfer; that recipient is disposable by design and is deliberately not
# listed, but the sending wallet is reused across the campaign.
# Source: OpenSourceMalware, "NullReceiver's Blank Crypto Transfers Solves the
# Challenges of EtherHiding", August 2026.
A10-npm3!
0xa322e5f3d311d3080e6f0121063e9adc2490ef1a

# The A8 campaign-marker assignment, written literally into the payload that is
# appended to a config file. Published as a grep-friendly signature in three
# forms -- global.i="A8-*#" for the fake-font variant, and global.i="A8-3292-1"
# and global.i="A8-3292-2" for the babel.config.cjs variant -- so the shared
# prefix is carried here instead of the three. Nothing legitimate assigns a
# string beginning "A8-" to global.i.
# Source: OpenSourceMalware, "NPM Isn't Prepared For North Korean PolinRider
# Attack", August 2026.
global.i="A8-

# The A8 marker again, in the other quote style. The entry above was taken from
# a sample written global.i="A8-3292-1". The September 2026 fake-font build
# opens its payload with global.i = 'A8'; -- single quotes, spaces around the
# '=' -- so the double-quoted prefix does not match it, and a build in a second
# repository carries the related marker A8-n*. Carried as its own prefix rather
# than by relaxing the other entry, because ioc/ is matched as fixed strings and
# cannot express "either quote".
# Source: OpenSourceMalware, "PolinRider is A/B Testing its Way Past Your
# Detections", September 2026.
global.i = 'A8

# The two XOR keys in the string table of the 500-variant fake-font payload,
# readable without deobfuscating the file. The second is carried as the
# whitespace-free tail of the published key: the source prints it inside a
# pre-formatted table as Sr3=@   y-p_>d$0B&@^1aQk, and the run of spaces cannot
# be distinguished from column alignment, so the part that can be established
# byte for byte is what is matched.
# Source: OpenSourceMalware, "PolinRider is A/B Testing its Way Past Your
# Detections", September 2026.
q4FZkxX{!h
y-p_>d$0B&@^1aQk

# The Ethereum dead-drop branch, from the 0x33ff operator wallet: the same
# technique as NullReceiver above -- the C2 address is read out of the recipient
# field of a heartbeat transaction -- but a different wallet, a different
# obfuscator and a different marker letter. The 32-hex string is the sender
# check the loader embeds verbatim (`var r = '33ff3eda...'`), and it is
# deliberately the truncated form: it also matches the full operator address
# 0x33ff3edaf55a8e03dcbc7cb40d498a49cd499891 and the `X:` request header, which
# the full address would not. `_$_fed0` is the string-table name of this build,
# the same shape as `_$_1e42` above. `global.o='5-` is the campaign-marker
# assignment with the counter dropped; the published markers are 5-841-du,
# 5-1169-du and 5-1460-du. Nothing legitimate assigns a "5-" string to global.o.
# Source: SafeDep, "PolinRider Switches to Ethereum C2 in 30+ Repositories",
# September 2026.
33ff3edaf55a8e03dcbc7cb40d498a49
_$_fed0
global.o='5-
YU7m{rE/>|==b>#~

# The second operator wallet again, in the checksummed mixed case the loader
# actually embeds. `ioc/` is matched with grep -F and no -i, so the lowercase
# entry earlier in this file does not match an infected file: the source prints
# the literal as '0xa322E5f3D311D3080e6f0121063e9aDC2490Ef1a'.toLowerCase(),
# and the OpenSSF record for `pybitjs` cites the same casing. Both forms are
# carried; neither subsumes the other.
# Source: as above. See docs-site/src/content/docs/indicator-reviews/2026-10-05.md.
0xa322E5f3D311D3080e6f0121063e9aDC2490Ef1a

# The first XOR key of the 0xa322 branch, complete. The 2026-09-28 entry read
# OpenSourceMalware's column-aligned table `q4FZkxX{!h,Sr3=@   y-p_>d$0B&@^1aQk`
# as two keys separated by that comma, and carried `q4FZkxX{!h` -- the part it
# could establish byte for byte -- for the first. This source prints the pair as
# two arguments in source code, rl(..., 'q4FZkxX{!h,Sr3=@', !1) and
# rl(..., 'y-p_>d$0B&@^1aQk', !0), so the comma is inside the first key and both
# keys are sixteen characters. The shorter entry above is a prefix of this one
# and is kept rather than replaced: it still matches, and it covers a build that
# reuses only the first half.
# Source: as above. See docs-site/src/content/docs/indicator-reviews/2026-10-05.md.
q4FZkxX{!h,Sr3=@

# confirmed by SafeDep as the 0xa322 C2 for 2026-08-22 to 2026-08-27, and the
# OpenSSF record for `pybitjs` cites the report as a reference.
test26330331/test

# The third operator wallet: the Ethereum sender whose transactions the loader
# reads for its C2, the same dead-drop technique as 0xa322 and 0x33ff above.
# Found in loaders in compromised GitHub repositories in October 2026 and in
# twelve releases of ten hijacked npm packages on 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-04.
# Carried in lower case, which is how all three sources print it and how the
# loader sends it to Blockscout; none of them prints the literal as the loader
# embeds it, so a checksummed mixed-case form may exist and is not carried.

# The first statement of the hijacked-npm loader, as it sits in the file: the
# loader is appended to the package's entry file as eval(atob("...")) after
# 131 or 157 tabs, and the blob opens Z2xvYmFsLmkgPSAnQTEwLW5wbV9pbmplY3Qn,
# which is base64 for global.i = 'A10-npm_inject'. The first sixteen characters
# are base64 for the twelve bytes of global.i = ' and so are the same whatever
# campaign tag follows; that prefix is what is carried. Nothing legitimate
# base64-encodes an assignment to global.i. The second entry is the tag itself,
# which the loader also sends as its Sec-V request header.
# Sources: Greenflagged, as above (the payload line is quoted from
# client-redux lib/index.js:292); OpenSSF malicious-packages MAL-2026-18643
# (`@adminide-stack/utils`; Amazon Inspector), 2026-11-04; Sonatype, as above.
Z2xvYmFsLmkgPSAn
A10-npm_inject

# Markers the second stage writes into the files it patches so it runs again:
# M260630A ends the snippet appended to npm's own lib/cli.js after 200 spaces,
# NPM_WS_SHIM marks the npm-cli.js shim dropped on Windows, RS260605 opens the
# 1.5 MB copy of the loader ("inz") written into npm and into the startup files
# of VS Code, Cursor, Antigravity, Discord and GitHub Desktop, and the five
# C-numbered markers are written by the same injection into those editor and
# app files. The npm program-file check reads this file, so the first three
# confirm a patched npm; nothing reads the editor files yet (see the entry).
